items.title: ITI Graduation Project - Full-Stack BI System

details.dataset: Real-world delivery company data across multiple platforms

Identified top-performing regions and underperforming platforms

items.title: ADAS Graduation Project
items.brief: AI-powered Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) integrating Driver Face Recognition, Driver Monitoring, Traffic Sign Recognition, and V2V communication using Computer Vision, Edge AI, and IoT technologies.

details.overview: An AI and IoT-based Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) developed as our Computer Engineering graduation project. The system enhances driving safety through Driver Face Recognition, Driver Monitoring, Traffic Sign Recognition, Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication, and a real-time dashboard powered by Firebase.
details.problem: Road accidents are often caused by driver fatigue, distraction, unauthorized vehicle access, missed traffic signs, and the lack of communication between nearby vehicles. The project addresses these challenges by combining Computer Vision, Edge AI, and V2V technologies into a unified safety system.
objectives: Authenticate drivers using facial recognition before vehicle operation.
Monitor driver attention and detect drowsiness in real time.
Recognize traffic signs using a YOLO-based object detection model.
Enable secure real-time V2V communication between vehicles.
Deploy AI models on edge devices for low-latency inference.
Provide live system monitoring through Firebase and a graphical dashboard.
details.dataset: Traffic Sign Recognition was trained using the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset. Driver Face Recognition relies on registered user images, while Driver Monitoring operates using real-time facial landmarks without requiring model training.
details.methodology: Driver authentication using face_recognition → Driver Monitoring using dlib facial landmarks and Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) → Traffic Sign Recognition using YOLOv8 on Raspberry Pi → Socket communication between Laptop and Raspberry Pi → SPI communication with ESP32 → Real-time system status synchronization via Firebase.
kpis: Real-time driver authentication before vehicle operation.
Real-time drowsiness and driver absence detection.
Real-time traffic sign recognition on Raspberry Pi.
Low-latency communication between AI modules and embedded hardware.
Live synchronization of system states and alerts through Firebase.
insights: Splitting AI workloads between the Laptop and Raspberry Pi improved overall system performance and resource utilization.
EAR-based driver monitoring provided an efficient lightweight solution for real-time drowsiness detection.
YOLOv8 enabled accurate real-time traffic sign recognition suitable for edge deployment.
Socket and SPI communication created a seamless pipeline between AI modules and embedded hardware.
challenges: Deploying computer vision workloads efficiently across heterogeneous hardware.
Maintaining real-time performance while running multiple AI modules simultaneously.
Synchronizing communication between Laptop, Raspberry Pi, ESP32, and Firebase.
Balancing inference speed and accuracy for edge deployment.

items.title: Heart Disease Risk Classifier
items.brief: End-to-end ML pipeline for heart disease risk prediction using UCI dataset, deployed as a Streamlit web app.

details.overview: A complete machine learning project from data preprocessing to deployment, predicting heart disease risk for real-time clinical decision support.
details.problem: Early detection of heart disease risk can save lives. This project explores automated risk classification from patient health data.
objectives: Build an accurate heart disease classifier
Deploy as an interactive web app
details.dataset: UCI Heart Disease Dataset — 303 patient records with 14 clinical features
details.methodology: EDA → Feature engineering → Scikit-learn pipeline → Model evaluation → Streamlit deployment
insights: Identified key predictors: chest pain type, max heart rate, ST depression
Achieved strong classification performance with optimized pipeline
challenges: Handling class imbalance
Selecting the most predictive features
Building an intuitive Streamlit UI

items.title: Customer Churn Prediction
items.brief: ML project predicting bank customer churn using 270,000+ records with XGBoost achieving 86% accuracy.

details.overview: End-to-end machine learning project for predicting customer churn using real-world banking data at scale.
details.problem: Banks lose significant revenue from churning customers. Early identification enables targeted retention strategies.
details.dataset: Real-world banking dataset with 270,000+ customer records and behavioral features
details.methodology: EDA → Data cleaning → Feature engineering & encoding → Model training → Evaluation → Comparison
insights: Account balance and product usage are top churn predictors
XGBoost significantly outperformed Logistic Regression
challenges: Processing 270,000+ records efficiently
Handling class imbalance in churn labels

items.title: NEAT Self-Driving Car Simulation
items.brief: AI simulation where virtual cars evolve driving strategies using NEAT evolutionary algorithm and neural networks over 10+ generations.

details.overview: A neural network evolution simulation where cars learn autonomous driving through the NEAT genetic algorithm.
details.problem: Demonstrating how evolutionary algorithms can solve complex autonomous driving behavior without pre-labeled training data.
details.dataset: Sensor-based fitness scoring from simulated environment
details.methodology: Simulation environment (Pygame) → NEAT genome initialization → Evolutionary training → Fitness evaluation → Generation evolution
insights: Cars successfully learned to avoid walls and navigate tracks after 10+ generations
NEAT efficiently explored diverse neural architectures
challenges: Designing a meaningful fitness function
Balancing exploration vs exploitation in NEAT

items.title: Graph Traversal Visualizer
items.brief: Interactive web app visualizing BFS and DFS graph traversal algorithms with real-time animations and dynamic graph support.

details.overview: An educational web tool that brings graph algorithms to life through real-time visual animations.
details.problem: Graph traversal algorithms are abstract and hard to intuitively understand from textbooks alone.
objectives: Visualize BFS and DFS in real-time
details.methodology: Flask backend → NetworkX graph processing → Real-time animation → JavaScript frontend
kpis: Support for dynamic graphs of arbitrary size
insights: Visual animations significantly improved algorithm comprehension
Optimized NetworkX processing for responsive UX
challenges: Synchronizing backend graph processing with frontend animations
Optimizing for large dynamic graphs
